work_items.title: Locale registry + culture-code rename + N-locale parity gate + placeholder JSON seed
acceptance_criteria: SUPPORTED_LOCALES in locales.ts lists all six culture codes {cs-CZ,en-US,ru-RU,uk-UA,fil-PH,de-DE} with nativeName; DEFAULT_LOCALE = 'cs-CZ'; LocaleCode type derived from the array (const assertion).

index.ts builds resources from the six imported JSONs keyed by culture code, init with lng: DEFAULT_LOCALE (static), fallbackLng: 'en-US', supportedLngs from SUPPORTED_LOCALES.map(l => l.code), interpolation.escapeValue false. NO browser detection in index.ts.
cs.json renamed to cs-CZ.json and en.json to en-US.json with identical content; every importer updated (index.ts, locales.parity.test.ts, auditEventLabel.test.ts, eventTimeline.test.ts).
PlatformScreen.test.tsx changeLanguage('cs') updated to changeLanguage('cs-CZ').

Four new files ru-RU.json, uk-UA.json, fil-PH.json, de-DE.json exist as key-complete copies of cs-CZ.json (placeholder Czech values); a new 'common.language' key is added to cs-CZ.json first and propagated to all locales so parity holds.

locales.parity.test.ts generalized: iterates the resources map exported from index.ts (imports that map, NOT each JSON individually — so parity itself carries zero per-locale literals), asserts every locale's flattened key set equals cs-CZ's, failing with the per-locale missing/extra key list; reuses existing flattenKeys.
index.ts exports the built resources map (keyed by culture code) so parity and any registry consumer read it instead of re-importing individual JSONs.

sentinelKeys.ts defines SENTINEL_KEYS: a curated frozen array of exactly six non-brand full-sentence dot-paths shared by all four language WIs — dispatcher: 'login.invalidCredentials', 'board.form.validation.phoneInvalid', 'settings.accessDenied'; customer: 'customer.order.loginPrompt', 'customer.tracking.cancelDialogBody', 'customer.login.codeMismatch'. It also exports ENFORCED_LOCALES (a LocaleCode[] the sentinel test iterates), seeded EMPTY in WI-1 so the four untranslated placeholder locales are not yet enforced and WI-1 stays GREEN; each language WI (WI-3..6) adds its own code to ENFORCED_LOCALES, giving that WI an observable RED (values still equal cs-CZ) → GREEN (real translation). Final state after WI-6 enforces all four. Do NOT add a static 'all four enforced' assertion to WI-1 — with the empty seed that would make WI-1 RED; enforcement accrues one locale per language WI and the conductor's full-suite gate exercises all four at the end.

locales.sentinel.test.ts: for each code in ENFORCED_LOCALES, asserts every SENTINEL_KEYS value in that locale's resources DIFFERS from the cs-CZ value (reads the index.ts resources map, resolving dot-paths); locales not in ENFORCED_LOCALES are skipped. With ENFORCED_LOCALES empty in WI-1, the suite is GREEN; the test carries no per-locale literals beyond consuming SENTINEL_KEYS + ENFORCED_LOCALES from sentinelKeys.ts.
test_cases: parity: each of the six locales has a key set identical to cs-CZ (iterate the resources map) — observe RED by adding a locale with a missing key, then GREEN once complete.

sentinel: with ENFORCED_LOCALES empty, locales.sentinel.test.ts is GREEN (no locale enforced); temporarily enforcing a placeholder locale shows RED (its sentinel values still equal cs-CZ), proving the gate bites before any WI-3..6 translation lands.
index.ts default: imported i18n singleton resolves i18n.language to 'cs-CZ' and t('app.title') returns the Czech string with no detection call.
eventTimeline + auditEventLabel tests still pass against the renamed cs-CZ.json / en-US.json paths.
PlatformScreen suite green after changeLanguage('cs-CZ').

work_items.title: Detection + persistence + switching runtime, main.tsx apply, formatting-stays-cs guard, Playwright locale pin
acceptance_criteria: languageStorage.ts uses the driverSettings.ts localStorage try/catch pattern, key 'app.language' (NOT in authStorage): getStoredLanguage() returns a LocaleCode validated against SUPPORTED_LOCALES or null; setStoredLanguage(code) writes; both swallow storage errors.

resolveInitialLanguage(navigatorLangs, stored) is pure: stored wins -> exact culture-code match -> primary-subtag match -> DEFAULT_LOCALE for unknown/empty. The primary-subtag map is DERIVED from SUPPORTED_LOCALES (code.split('-')[0] -> code: de->de-DE, uk->uk-UA, ru->ru-RU, en->en-US, cs->cs-CZ, fil->fil-PH); ONLY the tl->fil-PH legacy alias (Tagalog, not derivable) is hardcoded. A hypothetical 7th locale (e.g. es-ES) must auto-detect from 'es' with NO edit to resolveInitialLanguage.ts (AC#8).
applyInitialLanguage() resolves navigator.languages + stored, calls i18n.changeLanguage(code) and sets document.documentElement.lang; invoked once from main.tsx only, never from index.ts.

useLanguage() returns { current, setLanguage }; setLanguage(code) calls i18n.changeLanguage, setStoredLanguage, and sets document.documentElement.lang; react-i18next re-render switches all t() consumers with no reload.
main.tsx calls applyInitialLanguage() before render.
playwright.config.ts top-level use gains locale: 'cs-CZ' so Chromium navigator.language is cs-CZ and detection keeps every existing e2e spec in Czech.
formatStaysCs.test.ts: after i18n.changeLanguage('de-DE'), money.ts still renders 'Kč' / cs-CZ grouping and the date helper still formats in Europe/Prague (AC#6).
test_cases: resolveInitialLanguage: exact ['de-DE']->de-DE; primary-subtag ['de']->de-DE, ['tl']->fil-PH, ['fil']->fil-PH; stored-wins (stored 'ru-RU' beats navigator ['de'])->ru-RU; unknown ['ja']->cs-CZ; empty []->cs-CZ.
languageStorage: round-trip set/get; invalid stored value ('xx-YY') ignored -> null; getItem throwing -> null (safe); setItem throwing -> no throw.
useLanguage: setLanguage('de-DE') calls i18n.changeLanguage, persists via setStoredLanguage, sets documentElement.lang='de-DE'; current reflects i18n.language.
formatStaysCs: money formatCzk stays 'Kč'/cs-CZ and date helper stays Europe/Prague after switching UI language to de-DE (AC#6).

work_items.title: ru-RU.json full translation (formal customer / informal driver)
acceptance_criteria: ru-RU.json has all keys of cs-CZ.json (native-quality Russian), key structure identical.
Every {{placeholder}} preserved verbatim; brand/proper nouns and non-text tokens (app name, SMS, PWA, Kč, error-code-like values) left untranslated.
Register split honored: customer-facing formal Russian, driver-facing informal Russian, mirroring the cs vy/ty split.
The generalized parity test passes for ru-RU (no missing/extra keys).

'ru-RU' is added to ENFORCED_LOCALES in sentinelKeys.ts; the sentinel gate (locales.sentinel.test.ts) then requires every WI-1-defined SENTINEL_KEYS value in ru-RU to DIFFER from cs-CZ — observe RED against the placeholder seed BEFORE translating, GREEN after real Russian lands. Do not restate the sentinel key set; consume it from WI-1's sentinelKeys.ts.
test_cases: parity: ru-RU key set equals cs-CZ key set (generalized locales.parity.test.ts from WI-1).
sentinel: after adding 'ru-RU' to ENFORCED_LOCALES, locales.sentinel.test.ts asserts all SENTINEL_KEYS differ from cs-CZ for ru-RU — RED on the seed copy, GREEN after translation.

work_items.title: Shared LanguageSelector + placement in dispatcher, driver settings, customer header
acceptance_criteria: LanguageSelector.tsx is a styled native <select> (VehicleSelector.tsx pattern), min-height theme.touchTargets.min (>=48px), one <option> per SUPPORTED_LOCALES entry showing nativeName, value = i18n.language, onChange -> useLanguage().setLanguage.
Accessible name via aria-label={t('common.language')}; renders all six options; passes vitest-axe via the src/shared/test/axe helper.
Dispatcher: mounted in AppLayout <Nav> before the mute/logout controls.
Driver: mounted as a settings section in DriverSettingsPage (styled like NavAppPreference), not the bottom nav.
Customer: mounted in CustomerLayout header actions next to CallButton.
Component maps SUPPORTED_LOCALES only — no individual locale-code literals (AC#8).
test_cases: renders all six options with nativeName labels (getByRole('option')).
selecting an option calls setLanguage with the chosen code (i18n.changeLanguage + persist), verified via a spied/mocked useLanguage.
value reflects i18n.language.
axe: no violations (preconfigured helper).
AppLayout renders the selector; DriverSettingsPage renders the settings section; CustomerLayout renders it in the header next to CallButton.

work_items.title: Docs: i18n rule anchor, project-context note, decisions entry, AC#8 extensibility grep gate
acceptance_criteria: web-react-style.md#i18n-czech-first notes supported locales are defined by SUPPORTED_LOCALES, parity now covers all of them, and money/date formatting stays cs-CZ/Europe/Prague regardless of UI language.
00-PROJECT-CONTEXT.md records the six-locale set and the SUPPORTED_LOCALES source-of-truth.
docs/decisions.md records the six-locale decision, full-culture-code convention, and auto-detect -> Czech-fallback behavior.

AC#8 extensibility contract enforced by extensibility.test.ts: a scan of NON-TEST production source under web/src (exclude *.test.ts/*.test.tsx and the whitelist files locales.ts, index.ts, resolveInitialLanguage.ts, shared/date/analyticsRange.ts) flags ONLY the FIVE non-default culture codes {en-US, ru-RU, uk-UA, fil-PH, de-DE} and asserts none appears. 'cs-CZ' is DELIBERATELY EXEMPT from the scan: per the spec's formatting non-goal, 'cs-CZ' is spec-MANDATED as a formatting literal in ~30 non-test production files (money.ts Intl.NumberFormat('cs-CZ'), TrackingPage, HistoryRow, PlatformScreen, AuditPage, DriverDrilldown, smsCostDisplay, csvExport, etc.) — those are correct and MUST NOT be 'fixed'. shared/date/analyticsRange.ts is whitelisted because its Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', { timeZone: 'Europe/Prague' }) is a locale-agnostic date-parts extractor (NOT a UI-language reference) — the 'en-US' there is a formatting literal, not a supported-locale code. resolveInitialLanguage.ts is whitelisted because it hardcodes exactly one legacy alias (tl -> fil-PH); its primary-subtag map is otherwise derived from the registry.
The extensibility.test.ts source comment states WHY cs-CZ is exempt (formatting non-goal, ~30 mandated files) so an impl agent does not add cs-CZ back into the flagged set.

Adding a hypothetical 7th locale (es-ES) requires exactly: one xx-YY.json, one SUPPORTED_LOCALES entry, one import+resources line in index.ts — and NO edit to resolveInitialLanguage.ts (its subtag map derives from the registry) nor to the selector/parity (both read the registry).
test_cases: extensibility: scan of non-test production source asserts none of the five non-default culture codes {en-US, ru-RU, uk-UA, fil-PH, de-DE} appears outside the whitelist {locales.ts, index.ts, resolveInitialLanguage.ts, shared/date/analyticsRange.ts}; 'cs-CZ' is NOT in the flagged set (spec-mandated formatting literal) and analyticsRange.ts's en-US is a formatting literal not a UI-language code; selector maps SUPPORTED_LOCALES, parity iterates the index.ts resources map, detection derives its subtag map from the registry.
